doc.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Mickey and Sylvia and Doris Troy; his reputation
summary: He recalls re-recording Mickey and Sylvia's Love Is Strange in straight time and Doris Troy's Just One Look, and says hits earned him tolerance despite his mouth.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Can you — this might be a hard question — but can you remember any particular sessions, particular songs where this kind of thing happened?

“Love is Strange.” Yeah. See their first record, the first one that they did in the early fifties was mostly all swing. But it was re-recorded in ’60, ’61. I re-recorded it and brought it with a different sound. Almost straight. But if you hear the record that’s been played all these years, for the last forty years, it’s been their record of the straight time. Not the one that was the shuffle, but more of the straight time. Strings and all. The sound that they had with her moaning and doing two or three different sounds, having the background singers just follow her and not do things on their own. It made all the difference in the world. And that’s the one that’s been played for over forty years, that particular record. So I’ve been very pleased about things like that. “Just One Look,” was my biggest record.

It was a straight, you know? I mean we had no strings and horns and stuff like that. We had background singers. And I came in because they couldn’t find another drummer. They went around looking. This was a demo.

But those are the way things were happening and they were going on. So I got a chance to speak about what I was doing, what I would like to do and that was happening. And they allowed me to do it. So with all those years of running off at the mouth and all of a sudden records becoming hits, I got a reputation. So people gave me the benefit of the doubt of things that I was doing. I was doing something different. Yes he’s got a big mouth, but was making hit records.
So we could put up with it.

We’d put up with it. When the date was over it was over. They didn’t have to deal with me. They weren’t going home with me. They knew this. I mean it was a business to them. But I didn’t know. I didn’t know that I was even alienating people. I mean I was even doing that. Because yeah I got a little arrogant with it after a while. But my arrogance was not like I didn’t know what I was talking about. I was just happy. I was just a kid. I’m coming from nothing to coming to big time.
